sections.title: Belief, action, and secular ethics
sections.rationale: This exchange establishes whether conduct requires religious belief and whether contemplative practice can independently ground ethical behavior.

sections.title: Religious stories and cultural evolution
sections.rationale: This section tests whether inherited stories embody biologically and culturally selected responses to suffering or remain mixed and contestable memetic constructions.

sections.title: Secular societies and inherited morality
sections.rationale: The speakers directly contest empirical social outcomes and whether modern secular institutions remain dependent on inherited religious commitments.

sections.title: Tragedy and ultimate meaninglessness
sections.rationale: This exchange isolates whether meaning must sustain people through tragedy or whether acceptance of ultimate meaninglessness remains compatible with ordinary purpose.

sections.title: Constructed meaning and the God-function
sections.rationale: The concluding response chain tests whether enacted priorities refute lived meaninglessness, arise through cultural construction, or necessarily perform the function of God.
